introduction: A family session photographs everyone together at the stage you are in right now: the baby who has just learned to crawl, the teenager who still agrees to stand beside you, the grandparent who rarely gets a photograph with the whole family. It is for people who want pictures on a wall rather than lost in a phone.
This page explains how a session works with children, who can be included, how to choose a place and a season, and how to book a family photographer in London, Ontario.

sections.heading: Sessions with children of different ages
body: Children set the pace of a family session, and good planning works with that rather than against it. Babies do best after a feed and a nap, toddlers last longest early in the day, and older children relax when they are given something to do instead of something to pose. Plan for breaks, bring a snack and let the youngest wander for a few minutes, because the best photograph is often the one that follows the one that went wrong. [[CONFIRM: how the studio paces a session with young children and what happens when a child will not cooperate]].

sections.heading: Who is in the photographs
body: Family means different things in different homes. A session can be two parents and one child, three generations around a table or a household that includes a dog. Decide ahead of time who will be photographed and tell everyone the time and the place, since a missing grandparent is the omission people regret. [[CONFIRM: the maximum group size, whether the package price changes with it, and whether pets and newborns are welcome, with any age guidance]]. If one person dislikes being photographed, agree on a short, fixed number of frames.

sections.heading: Choosing a place and a season
body: A place that matters to the family often photographs better than a famous one: the park where the children learned to ride, the street you live on or the garden you tend. Season matters as much as place in Ontario, with leaf colour in autumn, blossom in spring and bright snow in winter, each of which also changes how long small children will tolerate being outside. The studio photographs families at [[CONFIRM: the places the studio uses, picked from this list of candidates: Meadowlily Woods, Fanshawe Conservation Area, Harris Park, Springbank Park with Storybook Gardens, Victoria Park, Wortley Village, Gibbons Park, a neighbourhood park; also any travel fee outside London]].

sections.heading: Clothes that work together
body: Aim for a palette rather than a uniform. Pick two or three colours that suit everyone's complexion, let each person wear a different shade of them, and keep patterns small or absent. Check that every outfit is comfortable for sitting on grass or climbing a fence, that shoes are clean and that nobody is wearing something new that itches. Children will tell you, loudly, when clothes are wrong, and photographs show it.

faqs.question: How many people can be in the session?
faqs.answer: A family session can be as small as one parent and a child or as large as several households. The size affects the pace and the choice of location more than anything else. [[CONFIRM: the maximum group size, and whether the starting price changes with the number of people]]. Say who is coming when you write, so the plan fits everyone.

faqs.question: Can our dog join the session?
faqs.answer: [[CONFIRM: whether pets are welcome, which kinds, and any conditions]]. If an animal is included, bring a lead or carrier, a favourite treat and a second adult whose only job is the animal, so the rest of the family can stay in the photograph.

faqs.question: What if my toddler will not cooperate?
faqs.answer: It happens at almost every session with a small child, and it is rarely a problem. Short stretches of photographing between breaks, a few minutes of free play and a calm adult kneeling beside them usually bring a toddler back. [[CONFIRM: how the studio handles a child who will not take part, and whether a session can be shortened or extended]].

faqs.question: When will we receive the photographs, and can I order prints?
faqs.answer: The package above sets out the edited photographs and the full set of originals you receive. Timing and extras are separate: [[CONFIRM: the delivery time and form, whether print or holiday-card options are offered, and any ordering deadline before the holidays]]. If you want cards or gifts by a particular date, say so when you book.

faqs.question: What if someone is ill or it rains?
faqs.answer: Illness and weather are the two most common reasons to move a family session, and moving it is better than photographing a miserable afternoon. [[CONFIRM: the studio's illness, rain and rescheduling policy, and what happens to any deposit]]. Let the studio know as early as you can.

faqs.question: When is the best time to book a family session?
faqs.answer: Book around a season you love or a moment worth marking: before the holidays, after a new arrival, ahead of a move, or while the grandparents are visiting. Starting from the date you need the photographs, work backwards. The studio's busiest months are [[CONFIRM: the busiest months and how far ahead to book]].

faqs.question: How do we book a family session?
faqs.answer: Write through the contact link below with the number of people, their ages, the season you hope for and any place you have in mind. The package above lists the starting price and its inclusions, and [[CONFIRM: deposit and cancellation terms]] are explained when you book.
